title: Jelly Roll's explanation: melody from New Orleans, beat from Latin America
summary: Thomas relays Jelly's view that jazz melody came from New Orleans and the beat from the Latin countries; Hinton argues the beat came from Africa.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Oh, and let me tell you another thing that I left out about Jelly. I had a little sense of asking him questions. And he liked me, and he'd tell me. And the one thing he told me about Jazz, he said, "The melody came from New Orleans, but the beat came from the Latin American countries." He said, "That's how the New Orleans music was so good, because those guys had the melody and the beat came up from the islands..."
Well, like they say, the beat came from Africa...
Well, that's where they come from...
That's where the Latin American countries got it.
But that's where New Orleans got it from. They got it from the Latin countries.
Well, what about the slaves that were down there?
Well, they were from Africa. They were from Africa.
Yeah, but that (?)got nothin' to do(?) with Latin America.
But see, wait a minute. Now, you've got to remember this. Jelly Roll came from a good family.
That's right.
Thomas - 73
And he studied music.
That's right.
And he was the first Jazz musician that knew how to write?
Write and read.

And he analyzed this thing. Because evidently, he must have gotten involved with going to one of them Latin countries, and them Africans in Cuba... The greatest experience I ever had in my life was playing with a Cuban band.
That's right. Because they got it from Africa!

Well, yeah. But he explained it from his standpoint. He didn't go all the way back to Africa when they come over here. He just know where they landed. Because they landed all in them Latin countries. And that's the way he explained Jazz to me. See, evidently, he...
The melody came from where? What did he say?

The melody came from New Orleans. And the guys in New Orleans had that sense of melody, he said. But the beat, where they got the beat from is from them South Americans. He put it in South America. He didn't go all the way back to Africa. Because I guess he just met them from South America. Because I often wondered how New Orleans had all that stuff going. And I've met so many guys
Thomas - 74
from New Orleans, and all of them had that same melody, same way of playing.
I agree with you.
